page: Amazon Web Services x2iezn.2xlarge is an x86_64 memory-optimized instance built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor. The system is powered by a dedicated Intel Xeon 8252C processor running at up to 4.5 GHz, delivering 4 physical cores and 8 vCPUs with 24 MB of L3 cache. It features an exceptionally high memory-to-compute ratio, supplying 256 GB of DDR4 RAM running at 3 GHz, which equates to 32 GB of memory per vCPU. The instance does not include bundled local storage, requiring network-attached storage, and provides a baseline network bandwidth of 12 Gbps. It contains no GPU hardware acceleration.

Benchmark results show strong single-threaded performance driven by the 4.5 GHz clock speed, with single-threaded gzip compression registering in the top 25% at 31.88 GB/sec. Memory bandwidth tests demonstrate 550.43 GB/sec on cached small blocks and 51.74 GB/sec on uncached large-block reads, supporting high-throughput memory operations such as 9.48 million Redis SET operations per second. However, total compute throughput remains constrained by the 8-vCPU allocation, as evidenced by average Geekbench multi-core scores of 5766.0 and lower comparative performance in multi-threaded decompression tests. Machine learning inference for medium-sized models is weak due to the absence of dedicated accelerators.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the hardware configuration provides extreme memory density without incurring the expense of unneeded compute cores. This makes the instance cost-effective for applications where RAM capacity drives resource sizing rather than parallel compute. The instance is primarily suited for large in-memory databases, electronic design automation (EDA) tooling, caching tiers, and relational database systems requiring heavy memory allocations.

The instance provides 256 GB of DDR4 system memory, achieving an extensive 32 GB per-vCPU ratio. It does not include local disk storage or GPU accelerators, relying on attached network storage alongside a 12 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. Benchmark data indicates strong single-threaded performance, with gzip compression reaching 31.88 GB/sec and Redis executing 9.48 million SET operations per second, while overall multi-threaded throughput reflects its 8-vCPU cap. This architecture allows organizations to provision large RAM capacities without paying for excessive CPU cores. The instance is suited for in-memory databases, EDA workloads, real-time analytics, and caching infrastructure.

256 GB high-speed DDR4 memory providing an extreme 32 GB per-vCPU ratio
